`Switch` is the part: one native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`, so it needs no `nativeButton`. Its types are `Switch.Props`, `Switch.State` and `Switch.ChangeEventReason`, and the flat names `SwitchProps`, `SwitchState` and `SwitchChangeEventReason`. `readonly` is in place of `readOnly`, and `value` and `form` are plain attributes. `focusableWhenDisabled` keeps a disabled switch in the tab order with `aria-disabled="true"`. The `element` of the template ref is the input, in place of `inputRef`. CSS selects `:checked`, `:disabled`, `:required`, `:focus`, `[aria-disabled="true"]`, `[aria-readonly="true"]` and `[aria-invalid="true"]`, so the input has no `data-checked`, `data-unchecked`, `data-filled`, `data-disabled`, `data-required`, `data-focused`, `data-readonly` and `data-invalid`.
An element of the developer beside the input, or the `element` slot with `state`, gives the thumb.
